meaning: Snare on beats 2 and 4 of a 4/4 bar.
Beats 2 and 4; usually where the snare or claps go.
Beats 1 and 3; usually where the kick goes.
Kick on every beat (1, 2, 3, 4), as in house and disco.
Beat 1 of the bar; also any main beat as opposed to an offbeat.
On beat 1, the first beat of the bar.
The & between beats: the second eighth note of a beat (& of 1, & of 2, ...).
The & of 2: halfway between beat 2 and beat 3. Speech recognition may write 'and' as 'end'.
Sixteenth-note counting is 1 e & a: e is the second sixteenth of a beat, & the third, a the fourth.
Triplet counting is 1 trip let: three even pulses per beat.
One hit per beat.
Two hits per beat: on the beat and the &.
Four hits per beat: 1 e & a.
Eight hits per beat.
One hit every two beats: beats 1 and 3 in 4/4.
One hit per bar, on beat 1.
Beats 1 and 3 in 4/4, or 2 and 4 if starting from 2.
A groove that feels half as fast at the same tempo: snare on beat 3 instead of 2 and 4. As a tempo request ('half time', 'half the speed') it can mean halving the BPM.
A groove that feels twice as fast: snare on every & or every beat. As a tempo request it can mean doubling the BPM.
Hits placed off the main beats, on &s, e's or a's.
A hit just before a beat, on the & or a of the previous beat.
A very quiet snare hit. This player has no dynamics, so ghost notes are ordinary snare hits.
A louder hit. This player has no dynamics.
A one-off drum variation at the end of a phrase. This player loops a single bar, so fills aren't supported.
Busy means more hits; sparse or stripped-down means fewer.
The repeating drum pattern of one bar.
One cycle of the beats per bar.
The kick lane.

term: snare, rimshot, cross-stick, side stick, clap
meaning: The snare lane; claps and rimshots also go here.

term: hi-hat, hat, hats, closed hat, open hat, ride, cymbal, shaker
meaning: The hat lane; ride and other timekeeping cymbals go here.
Not available; the player only has kick, snare and hat.
Delaying every second subdivision for a lilting, triplet-like feel. Shuffle is heavy swing.
No swing; evenly spaced subdivisions.
Three subdivisions per beat.
Four beats per bar.
Three beats per bar, accent on 1.
Two dotted-quarter pulses per bar with three subdivisions each: 2 beats, 3 subdivisions.
Four dotted-quarter pulses with three subdivisions each: 4 beats, 3 subdivisions.
Five or seven beats per bar.
Seven eighth notes per bar, usually counted as 7 beats.
Two half-note beats per bar: 2 beats, 2 subdivisions.
Counting 'one, two, three, four' before the music starts, which sets the tempo.
Beats per minute; this player supports 20 to 320.
Plain click sounds without a drum pattern (click mode).
Drum mode: the kick, snare and hat grid plays.
3+3+2 pattern: hits on 1, & of 2 and 4 in 4/4 (positions 0, 1.5, 3).
Son clave over two bars; in one bar of 4/4 the 3-side is 1, & of 2, 4.
Reggae: kick and snare together on beat 3 only, nothing on 1.
Offbeat chops on every &.
Hip-hop: kick on 1 (and often the & of 2 or 3), snare on 2 and 4.
Country: steady snare eighths or sixteenths with kick on 1 and 3.
Twice as many hat hits, e.g. eighths become sixteenths.

term: move it back, move it forward
meaning: Back means earlier in the bar, forward means later.
